translation_en: Maymunah reported that a mouse fell into clarified butter. The Prophet said, Remove it and the butter around it, then eat the rest. The report is transmitted by Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, from Maymunah.

Ibn Umar disliked branding images and said the Prophet forbade striking or branding an image. Qutaybah reported the same wording from al-Anqazi and Hanzalah. Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated it from Hanzalah, from Salim, from Ibn Umar. Qutaybah also reported the wording from Hanzalah that an image should not be struck.

Anas said he brought a brother to the Prophet for tahnik. While in his sheep pen, the Prophet branded a sheep, apparently on its ear. Hisham bin Zayd narrated that he entered with Anas to visit the Prophet, who was in his sheep pen.

Rafi bin Khadij said they would meet the enemy the next day without knives. The Prophet said to use anything that makes the blood flow and has Allah's name mentioned, except a tooth or nail: a tooth is bone, and a nail is the knife of the Abyssinians. People hurried ahead and set cooking pots while the Prophet was behind them, so he ordered them emptied. He divided the spoils, valuing one camel at ten sheep. One camel escaped, and a man stopped it with an arrow. The Prophet said these animals can bolt like wild animals, so deal with one this way. The chain is Musaddad, Abu al-Ahwas, Said bin Masruq, Abayah bin Rifaa, from his father, from his grandfather Rafi bin Khadij.

Rafi said a camel escaped during a journey and a man stopped it with an arrow. The Prophet said to handle escaping camels as one would wild animals. Rafi asked about slaughter when they had no knives; the Prophet said to use anything that makes the blood flow with Allah's name, but not a tooth or nail. The report was related by Ibn Salam, from Umar bin Ubaid al-Tanafisi, from Said bin Masruq, from Abayah bin Rifaa, from Rafi bin Khadij. Rafi described both the escaped camel and their need to slaughter while traveling without knives.

Al-Bara reported that the Prophet said they should first pray that day, then return and slaughter. Whoever did so followed their practice; slaughter before prayer was merely meat for one's family, not a sacrifice. Abu Burdah had already slaughtered and had a young goat. The Prophet told him to slaughter it, but said it would not count for anyone after him. Another version says slaughter after prayer completes the rite and follows the Muslims' practice. Al-Bara said the Prophet told Abu Burdah to slaughter the young goat he had, but it would not count for anyone else. Mutarrif also reported from Amir, from al-Bara, that slaughter after prayer completes the rite and follows the Muslims' practice.

Anas reported that whoever slaughters before prayer has slaughtered for himself; whoever slaughters after prayer completes the rite and follows the Muslims' practice. The Prophet distinguished slaughter before prayer, which is only for the person and family, from slaughter after prayer, which completes the sacrifice and follows the Muslims' practice.

Uqbah bin Amir received a young goat when the Prophet distributed sacrificial animals. He asked about it, and the Prophet told him to sacrifice it. Uqbah bin Amir said the Prophet distributed the sacrifices to his Companions, and a young goat came to Uqbah.

Aishah was menstruating at Sarif before they entered Mecca and was crying. The Prophet said menstruation is something Allah prescribed for the daughters of Adam. She should do what pilgrims do, but not circumambulate the House. At Mina she was served cow meat and was told the Messenger had sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives. Aishah said this happened at Sarif before they entered Mecca. The Prophet explained that menstruation is decreed for the daughters of Adam, and allowed her to perform the pilgrimage rites other than circumambulating the House.

Anas bin Malik reported that on the Day of Sacrifice the Prophet said, Whoever has slaughtered before the prayer must slaughter again. A man stood and said, Messenger of Allah, this is a day when people want meat, and he mentioned his neighbors. I have a young goat better than two sheep kept for meat. The Prophet allowed him to slaughter it, but Anas was unsure whether that permission extended to anyone else. The Prophet then turned to two rams and slaughtered them. The people went to a small flock and divided it among themselves.

Abu Bakra reported that the Prophet said time has returned to how it was when Allah created the heavens and earth. A year has twelve months, four sacred: three consecutive months, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Shaban. The Prophet asked which month, land, and day they were; each time they replied that Allah and His Messenger knew best. He identified Dhu al-Hijjah, the Sacred City, and the Day of Sacrifice. He said their blood, property, and—Muhammad thought he also said—honor are sacred, like that day, city, and month. They will meet their Lord, who will ask about their deeds. He warned them not to return to misguidance and kill one another, and told those present to convey the message to those absent, who might understand it better. Muhammad said the Prophet spoke the truth and repeated, Have I not conveyed the message? Muhammad bin Salam narrated it from Abd al-Wahhab, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Bakrah, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet. The four sacred months include three consecutive ones and Rajab of Mudar. The Prophet emphasized the sanctity of blood, wealth, and honor, warned the community not to fight one another after him, and repeatedly asked whether he had delivered the message.

Nafi reported that Abdullah used to slaughter at the place of slaughter. Ubaidullah explained that it was the Prophet's place of slaughter. Ubaidullah explained Nafi's wording as referring to the Prophet's own place of slaughter. He used this location for the ritual sacrifice.
Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger used to slaughter at the prayer place. Ibn Umar reported this practice of the Messenger of Allah. The report was narrated by Ibn Umar.

Anas said the Prophet sacrificed two rams, and Anas did the same. Anas said he also sacrificed two rams, following the Prophet's practice. He reported this as the Prophet's own practice of offering two rams.

Anas reported that the Messenger turned to two horned, white-and-black rams and slaughtered them with his own hand. Other narrators transmitted the same account through Ayyub. Anas reported that the Messenger slaughtered the two rams himself. Wuhaib followed Ayyub with this narration; Ismail and Hatim bin Wardan also reported it from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas.

Uqbah bin Amir said the Prophet gave him sheep to distribute as sacrifices. One young goat remained, so Uqbah asked about it. The Prophet told him to sacrifice it. The Prophet had given Uqbah sheep to divide among his Companions as sacrifices. When a young goat remained, he told Uqbah to sacrifice it himself.

Al-Bara said his maternal uncle Abu Burdah had slaughtered before prayer. The Prophet said his sheep counted only as meat. Abu Burdah had a domesticated young goat, so the Prophet allowed him to slaughter it, but not as a valid sacrifice for anyone else. He said slaughter before prayer is for oneself; slaughter after prayer completes the rite and follows the Muslims' practice. The narrators differed in describing the animal's age. The Prophet said that sacrifice after prayer completes the rite and follows the Muslims' practice. Other transmitters differed over whether Abu Burdah had a young goat, a young she-goat, or another young animal, and whether it was better than an older sheep. They also differed in the exact description of its age.

Al-Bara said Abu Burdah slaughtered before prayer, so the Prophet told him to replace it. Abu Burdah had only a young goat, which he thought better than an older sheep. The Prophet told him to use it, but it would not count for anyone after him. Another chain from Anas also described the animal as a young goat. The report is from Muhammad bin Bashshar, Muhammad bin Jafar, Shubah, Salamah, Abu Juhaifah, and al-Bara. Hatim bin Wardan also related the report from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Anas.
Anas said the Prophet sacrificed two white-and-black rams and placed his foot on their sides, invoking Allah and saying Allahu akbar as he slaughtered them himself.

Aishah said the Messenger came to her at Sarif while she was crying because her period had begun. He said this was something Allah prescribed for the daughters of Adam. She could do what pilgrims do, except circumambulate the House. The Messenger sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives. Aishah described the same pilgrimage guidance and added that the Prophet sacrificed cows on behalf of his wives.

Al-Bara reported that the Prophet said they should begin that day with prayer, then return and slaughter. Whoever slaughtered before prayer had only provided meat for his family, not performed the sacrifice. Abu Burdah said he had slaughtered early and had a young goat better than an older sheep. The Prophet told him to replace it, but said it would not suffice for anyone after him. The report is from Hajjaj bin al-Minhal, from Shubah, from Zubayd, who heard al-Shabi, from al-Bara.

Anas reported that whoever slaughters before prayer must slaughter again. A man said he wanted meat that day and had a young goat better than two older sheep. The Prophet allowed him to slaughter it, though the narrator was unsure whether the allowance was conveyed. He then slaughtered two rams, and people slaughtered from a small flock. The Prophet initially told him to repeat the sacrifice. The man explained that he wanted meat for his neighbors and had a young goat better than two older sheep. The Prophet permitted him, though the narrator was unsure whether this permission extended to others.
Jundab bin Sufyan said he witnessed the Prophet on the Day of Sacrifice. The Prophet said whoever slaughtered before prayer must replace it with another, and whoever had not slaughtered should do so.

Al-Bara said the Prophet prayed, then said whoever prayed their prayer and faced their qiblah should not slaughter until he had finished. Abu Burdah said he had already done so and had a young goat better than two older sheep. The Prophet allowed him to slaughter it, but said it would not count for anyone after him. Amir said it was his best sacrificial animal.

Anas reported that the Prophet sacrificed two horned, white-and-black rams, placing his foot on their sides and slaughtering them with his own hand. Anas said the Prophet placed his foot on the sides of both rams and slaughtered them himself.
Anas said the Prophet sacrificed two horned, white-and-black rams with his own hand, invoking Allah and saying Allahu akbar, with his foot on their sides.

Masruq asked Aishah about a man sending a sacrificial animal to the Kaaba and staying at home, believing he must remain in ihram until the pilgrims finish. Aishah said she used to twist garlands for the Prophet's sacrificial animals, which he sent to the Kaaba; he did not avoid what was lawful for him with his family until the people returned. Aishah said she used to twist garlands for the Prophet's sacrificial animals, which he sent to the Kaaba. He remained at home and did not treat lawful relations with his family as prohibited until the people returned.

Jabir said that during the Prophet's time they took sacrificial meat with them as provisions to Medina, sometimes described as meat of the animals brought for pilgrimage. Jabir reported this practice during the Prophet's lifetime. He said the meat was referred to as both sacrificial meat and the meat of the animals offered for pilgrimage.

Abu Said returned from being away and was served meat. Told it was from their sacrifices, he asked them to set it aside, as he would not eat it. He went to his maternal brother Qatadah, who had attended Badr, and mentioned this. Qatadah said something had happened after Abu Said had left. Abu Said said he was absent, returned, and was offered meat. When told it was from their sacrifices, he refused to taste it and went to his maternal brother Qatadah, who had attended Badr. Qatadah told him that a ruling had changed after his absence.

Salamah bin al-Akwa reported that the Prophet said whoever sacrificed should not have any of it left at home after the third night. The following year they asked whether to do the same. He said to eat, feed others, and store some, because people had suffered hardship the previous year and he wanted them to help.
